budget_items.what_was_said: The repair to a badly rusted coupling at the Dana Street pump station was completed using FY25 money before the fiscal year closed, narrowly avoiding a system failure.
The business manager reported all required commissioner signatures were obtained and the FY25 adjustments are ready for final approval, having been delayed by a missing signature.
The chair proposed a flat inspection fee for accessory dwelling units to cover checking the external plumbing connection from the ADU into the existing house's line.
The chair cited Leominster's practice of charging a flat per-bedroom fee when a bedroom is added to an existing house, as a possible model distinct from the ADU fee.

A commissioner recalled that Wright-Pierce's typical annual charges had run in that range in past years, well below the current bill tied to the new NPDES permit mapping requirements, and asked whether the current cost was a one-time remap or a recurring annual charge.
The business manager said billing will go out in a couple of weeks, pending Leominster, for the current year's first-quarter billing.

decisions.decision: A wording correction (from 'effort' to 'effect') was identified in the July 8 minutes and agreed to be fixed before the vote to approve them.
Bill Bernard will recuse himself from voting on the Massachusetts Avenue easement matter because he was contracted by the homeowner for the original sewer install before joining the commission.
Only one or two commissioners will attend the August 21 meeting with town counsel on ADU/easement regulations, to avoid triggering public-meeting quorum requirements.
Wright-Pierce will be asked to help fill in the gaps in the NPDES permit response, per their proposal.
Dana Street is being dropped from future agendas since the repair is complete; the manhole IFB, ADU fee discussion, easements, and NPDES permit will remain standing agenda items.
Set the next meeting dates as August 12, August 26, September 9, and September 30, 2025, alternating regular DPW hybrid meetings and Zoom-only meetings.

minutes.headline: Sewer Commission weighed a flat ADU inspection fee and costly new NPDES mapping rules; no votes taken on either.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission reviewed completed Dana Street pump repairs and ongoing manhole rehabilitation, then turned to two bigger open items: a proposed flat fee for connecting accessory dwelling units to the sewer system, and a new MassDEP NPDES permit requiring costly annual system mapping work through engineering firm Wright-Pierce. Only routine procedural votes (minutes, adjournment) were taken; the ADU fee, easement policy for a Massachusetts Ave subdivision dispute (from which Bill Bernard will recuse), and the NPDES mapping cost questions were all left for further discussion and a planned meeting with town counsel on August 21.

what_happened.line: The commission left a proposed flat fee for ADU sewer connections undecided, with no vote taken.
It referred a new NPDES permit's annual system-mapping requirement to engineering firm Wright-Pierce rather than setting a cost or schedule.
Only one or two commissioners plan to attend an August 21 meeting with town counsel on ADU and easement rules, to avoid triggering public-meeting quorum.
Commissioner Bill Bernard will recuse himself from a Massachusetts Avenue easement dispute because he was contracted for the original sewer install there.
The Dana Street pump station repair, completed with FY25 funds before the fiscal year closed, is being dropped from future agendas.

why_it_matters: A flat ADU sewer-connection fee, once set, would become a new cost for any homeowner adding an accessory dwelling unit tied into town sewer.
The NPDES mapping mandate could raise sewer department costs, and sewer department costs are typically recovered through sewer fees rather than the tax levy.
How the commission staffs its August 21 meeting and who recuses on the Massachusetts Ave easement case shapes how openly those decisions get made.
